title: Unraveling the Effect of COVID-19 on the Selection of Optimal Portfolio Using Hybrid Quantum-Classical Algorithms
journal_or_venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE)
abstract_summary: This conference paper applies hybrid quantum-classical algorithms (VQE and QAOA) to portfolio optimization across pre-COVID and COVID-affected time windows using stock data from multiple industries and compares results to classical Markowitz modern portfolio theory. The authors report qualitative agreement between quantum approaches and Markowitz in identifying optimal portfolios, but note shortcomings in the ansatz and coefficient (weight) estimation from the quantum algorithms; they also observe sectoral COVID impacts (IT outperformance, energy underperformance) and recovery trends in late 2020.
methodology_description: The authors performed an empirical study comparing classical mean-variance (Markowitz MPT) portfolio optimization with hybrid quantum-classical approaches (VQE and QAOA) across multiple market periods to assess the impact of COVID-19. They collected historical equity price data for a set of representative firms across sectors (retail & e-commerce, technology, automotive, oil & gas, airways & hospitality) from Yahoo Finance, partitioning the timeline into three 24-month windows (2016-01-01 to 2017-12-31; 2018-01-01 to 2019-12-31; 2020-01-01 to 2021-12-31). For each asset universe and time window they computed return statistics consistent with Markowitz mean-variance theory (implied: returns and covariance/variance) and formulated the portfolio selection problem in a form amenable to quantum optimization (encoded as a Hamiltonian / cost operator). They then used Qiskit to implement VQE and QAOA hybrid algorithms (quantum state ansatz + classical optimizer for VQE; alternating operator ansatz for QAOA) to find low-energy eigenstates / high-cost bitstrings corresponding to candidate optimal portfolios. Results from the quantum runs (eigenvalues/energies, measured bitstring probabilities) were compared to the classical Markowitz-optimal portfolios computed in Python/Qiskit. Analysis focused on the selected asset combinations per period and sector, eigenvalue degeneracies, and measured probability distributions to assess correspondence and limitations (notably, that ansatz/probability amplitudes did not always match the classical weightings).
experimental_setup: Quantum experiments were implemented using IBM's Qiskit (no specific QPU or simulator backend explicitly stated). Classical computations (Markowitz MPT) were performed in Python. Data were obtained from Yahoo Finance. The paper does not specify whether runs used Qiskit local statevector/simulator backends or cloud QPUs, nor does it list numerical hyperparameters (shots, optimizer choice, ansatz type, QAOA depth).
dataset_used: Historical equity price data downloaded from Yahoo Finance for a selected set of stocks spanning five sectors (Retail & E-comm, Technology, Automotive, Oil & Gas, Airways & Hospitality). The analysis used three 24-month windows: 2016-01-01 to 2017-12-31 (Non-COVID-1), 2018-01-01 to 2019-12-31 (Non-COVID-2), and 2020-01-01 to 2021-12-31 (COVID). Stocks included tickers such as COST, AMZN, TGT, WMT, GOOG, IBM, INTC, MSFT, GM, DMLRY, TSLA, F, SHEL, COP, MRO, CVX, MAR, CHH, LTC, ALK (as listed in the paper).

steps: 1) Download historical price data from Yahoo Finance for each ticker and time window.
2) Compute return time series and covariance/variance statistics for each asset universe (mean-variance inputs).

3) Formulate the portfolio optimization problem per Markowitz MPT (mean-variance) and translate/encode that objective into a quantum cost Hamiltonian / QUBO suitable for VQE and QAOA (binary selection representation: bitstrings denote buy/hold choices).

4) Implement VQE in Qiskit: prepare parameterized ansatz state, evaluate energy expectation ⟨Ψ(θ)|H|Ψ(θ)⟩, use a classical optimizer to minimize energy; record resulting eigenvalues, eigenstates and measurement probabilities.

5) Implement QAOA in Qiskit: prepare alternating operator ansatz, optimize parameters to maximize expected cost ⟨C⟩, sample final state to obtain bitstring probabilities and identify candidate portfolios.
6) Compute classical Markowitz-optimal portfolios in Python/Qiskit to serve as baseline.

7) Compare quantum-generated candidate portfolios (eigenstates/bitstrings, energies, probabilities) against classical Markowitz solutions across sectors and time windows; analyze degeneracies, probability distributions and sector-level trends (impact of COVID-19).

[supported] QAOA likewise returned multiple portfolio bitstrings with nearly equal probabilities (i.e., nearly uniform coefficients), producing candidate portfolios that conflict with the single optimal-weight solution of classical Markowitz in the experiments performed.

[supported] The COVID-19 period (defined by the paper as 01-01-2020 to 12-31-2021) exhibited increased market volatility and sector-differentiated impacts that affected optimal-portfolio choices in the authors' experiments.

results_summary: The study applied hybrid quantum-classical algorithms (VQE and QAOA) to small portfolio optimization problems across pre-COVID and COVID-era 24-month windows and compared outcomes to classical Markowitz mean-variance solutions. Empirically, both VQE and QAOA identified low-energy portfolio bitstrings that qualitatively correspond to Markowitz-optimal portfolios, and sector-level COVID impacts observed (IT outperformance, energy underperformance) align with market behavior. However, the quantum runs produced amplitude/probability distributions (coefficients) that did not reflect classical portfolio weights: VQE showed nearly-degenerate eigenstates with very different probabilities, while QAOA returned several bitstrings with nearly equal probabilities. The authors interpret this as a need to improve problem encoding/ansatz rather than evidence of a clear quantum advantage.
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper does not demonstrate a computational or solution-quality advantage of quantum algorithms over classical methods. Instead, it reports qualitative agreement in identified candidate portfolios but highlights mismatches in amplitude/probability (weight) assignments, concluding that encoding/ansatz improvements are needed before any advantage can be claimed.
limitations: Ansatz and problem formulation limitations explicitly acknowledged by authors: the VQE/QAOA ansatz and objective-function formulation do not evaluate portfolio coefficients (weights) in a way that matches classical Markowitz outputs.

Degenerate / nearly-degenerate eigenstates with mismatched sampling probabilities: VQE produced almost-degenerate eigenvalues but highly skewed probabilities, and QAOA produced several states with almost-equal probabilities — leading to ambiguity in portfolio selection compared to classical Markowitz.

key_ideas: #idea:hybrid-approach — Applies hybrid VQE and QAOA implementations in Qiskit to map Markowitz mean-variance portfolio selection into a quantum cost Hamiltonian / QUBO and search for low-energy portfolio bitstrings using a classical optimizer.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Empirical study across three 24-month windows (pre- and during-COVID) indicates qualitative agreement between hybrid quantum approaches and classical Markowitz solutions on small asset universes, suggesting potential NISQ-era applicability for exploratory portfolio selection.

#idea:hybrid-approach — Quantum runs produced eigenstates/eigenvalues that match classical-optimal energies, but the measured probability amplitudes (ansatz coefficients) did not reproduce classical continuous weight allocations, highlighting a mismatch between bitstring selection and classical weightings.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Sector-level insights (IT outperformance, energy underperformance, recovery trends in late 2020) are observable when comparing quantum-derived candidate portfolios across time windows, indicating the method can capture broad market effects.

#limitation:simulation-only — The paper does not specify Qiskit backend (simulator vs cloud QPU), nor lists shots, ansatz details, QAOA depth, optimizer or qubit counts, making it likely results are from simulation and reducing reproducibility.
#limitation:no-empirical-validation — Missing concrete algorithm hyperparameters and hardware details limits validation and prevents assessment of real-hardware feasibility or noise impacts.
contradictions: The paper finds that VQE/QAOA can produce low-energy eigenstates matching the classical Markowitz optimum in energy but that measured bitstring probabilities and ansatz-derived coefficients do not align with classical continuous portfolio weights — contradicting any claim that current hybrid quantum methods directly reproduce or outperform classical MPT weight allocations.

By reporting qualitative agreement but highlighting ansatz and coefficient estimation shortcomings, the work challenges simplistic claims of near-term quantum superiority for portfolio-weight estimation without careful consideration of encoding/ansatz limitations and measurement-to-weight mapping.
